newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 14.

text.p: Criticism engulfs new super details: Opposition parties reacted with a fresh torrent of criticism when Treasurer Winston Peters gave more details of the proposed compulsory superannuation scheme on Tuesday. Page 1.

Valuation NZ to become crown-owned company: The Coalition Government has decided to turn Valuation NZ into a crown-owned company, just nine months after the previous National government decided it should remain a government department. Page 2.
Bradford bemoans firms' behaviour: Energy Minister Max Bradford said he was saddened by the "deliberately anti-competitive behaviour" of some power companies. Page 2.
Anti-crime bill rejected: The government would not support Labour MP Mike Moore's National Crime Authority Bill, Police Minister Jack Elder said on Tuesday. Page 2.

Hainz-Wattie cuts back in Gisborne: Heinz-Wattie announced the closure of its petfood and prepared foods operations in Gisborne on Tuesday, and said it was looking for a "strategic partner" to take over the frozen corn operation there. Page 17.
Tradenz should have used an outside auditor to investigate allegations of fraud by two staff members, the foreign affairs, defence and trade select committee says. Page 19.
Offer made to sell station: Radio Network will sell one of the three frequencies owned by Christchurch rival C93FM if it is allowed to buy the station. Page 19.

PM tries to calm super adversaries: The Prime Minister is trying to reduce friction between senior cabinet ministers over compulsory superannuation to stop their personal differences of opinion further destabilising the coalition.
IRD seeks taxes from CHH on winebox deal: The Inland Revenue Department has made two assessments against Charter Holt Harvey over winebox deals using the "anti-avoidable" provisions.

Merger not likely to spark fast changes: Any rationalisation in the New Zealand distribution of wines and spirits resulting from the merger between Guinness and Grand Metropolitan is not likely to happen quickly.
Chinese firm set to seal NZ engine deal: A Chinese company said on Tuesday it was satisfied with a revolutionary New Zealand-designed engine and was preparing to finalise a deal.

Subsidy key to GP visits for children: The coalition's vow to provide free GP visits for young children is now dependent on the willingness of doctors to hold consulting fees at or below the new $32.50 subsidy. Page 3.
Firestone to go non-stop: Firestone New Zealand has won its battle to run its tyre making plant in Christchurch seven days a week. Page 31.
